title: The Hierarchy of Needs for Training Dataset Development: Chang She and Noah Shpak
talk_summary: A talk about training-dataset development for LLMs, covering data quality hierarchies, synthetic data, quality classifiers, and the Lance columnar format for fast random access and cheap shuffling.

takeaways.what_they_do: They start every data effort from evaluations because it is the only way to measure whether data changes help; without it you cannot tell if a change is an improvement.
takeaways.evidence_quote: for us we always start there because it's hard to measure anything without a compass

takeaways.technique: Separate data materialization from the job
takeaways.what_they_do: They make dataset materialization a separate service with a stable interface (request in, file list out) so training jobs do not embed fragile data-format logic.
takeaways.evidence_quote: separating concerns in terms of how your data is materialized and what your training job is doing is really really nice for us

takeaways.technique: Versioned, time-travelable data with cheap rollback
takeaways.what_they_do: Lance format auto-versions data and supports instant rollback to a known-good version, plus zero-copy schema evolution for experimental columns.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's instantaneous to roll back to a previously known good version so that it doesn't corrupt down Downstream

takeaways.what_they_do: They shuffle references to rows rather than the rows themselves, saving iteration time on large datasets.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it essentially lets you Shuffle references to rows rather than shuffling the rows themselves

takeaways.what_they_do: They build classifiers for data quality, often just by prompting an LLM rather than training a model, to score and select data.
takeaways.evidence_quote: there's a lot of cool work around how people are actually doing this with just prompting classifications
